summary: Albrecht Wezler was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme (~1960–1965). He served as professor and director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and director at the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs by 2016, and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design in 2019.

Alessandro Graheli is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. In 2022, he was attested as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and as a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Alex McKay is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995. He held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his BA at Oxford and MA at SOAS, studying under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard University, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman (1921–2004) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. After studying at UCLA and UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray Barnson Emeneau, he taught at Wisconsin, Michigan, and Columbia University (1967–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He was a founding member of the Translation Bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1979).

Alexander C. Soper (1904–1993) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (~1939–1960) and New York University (~1960–1981).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös (1784–1842) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Bethlen Gábor College and the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn. He served as librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1831 and from 1837 to 1841.

Alexander Cunningham (1814–1893) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Christ's Hospital, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep. He served as archaeological surveyor for the Government of India and as director-general of the Archaeological Survey of India.
Alexander Duff (1806–1878) was a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He completed his education at the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829) and the University of Aberdeen.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1903–1907) and Christian Bartholomae (~1906–1908).

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., Janet Gyatso, and Robert H. Sharf. He holds a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander Hamilton (1762–1824) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature at the East India Company College beginning in 1806 and 1808.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has been a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and held a post as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied law at the University of Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He served as chief justice on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2003) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. By 2000, he held posts as a senior researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and as head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek (1802–1870) was a linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, becoming a full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden University in 1999.
Alexander Murray (1775–1813) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1794–1806) and later held a post there (~1812–1813).
